title: Reservoir controller: adaptive throughput headroom & safety envelope
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and implement a new autoscaling policy engine ("Reservoir Controller") for Dedicated pools that targets throughput headroom (quantile-based), integrates a cost-aware attenuation function for scale magnitude, and enforces multi-layer safety envelopes (tenant caps, global surge budget, cooldown). Goal: provide predictable throughput guarantees while limiting expensive over-provisioning and avoiding cascade oscillations.
target_metrics: Primary: p95 request-latency-at-target-qps per model-route (observed vs. SLA)
Secondary: observed throughput (tokens/sec) and request queue length
Stability: rate of instance additions/removals per 10m window
Cost proxy: node-hours and estimated GPU-token-cost delta after scaling
proposed_algorithm: Maintain a per-tenant 'headroom reservoir' expressed as target spare throughput (tokens/sec) computed from historical QPS and recent 99th traffic percentile
Continuously estimate short-term demand using EWMA with two horizons (30s and 5m) to detect spikes vs. demand shifts
Compute desired capacity delta = f(headroom_deficit, cost_gradient) where cost_gradient penalizes large immediate scale-ups to avoid overshoot
Apply attenuation curve: small deficits -> proportional add; large deficits -> staged ramp with minimum step size and enforced cool-down windows
Enforce safety envelope checks (per-tenant node_cap, global_surge_reserve, and rollout rate limits) before making allocation changes
Provide graceful fallback: if immediate capacity unavailable, trigger admission control path (priority-aware shedding or degraded mode) and emit diagnostic traces
safety_limits: Per-tenant node cap: hard limit on concurrent additional GPUs to prevent noisy neighbors
Global surge reserve: a cluster-wide budget (percentage of total pool) that can be consumed only when burst risk score > threshold
Cooldown policy: scale-up and scale-down cooldown windows are asymmetric (scale-down cooldown > scale-up cooldown) to reduce oscillation
Min-instance floor: do not reduce below a configured baseline instances for critical tenants
Max-change-per-interval: limit on number of nodes added/removed per 10m to preserve scheduling stability
decisions: Use quantile-based latency-to-throughput mapping (p95->qps) rather than average QPS to define headroom because tail latency drives SLA breaches
Adopt staged ramping with attenuation curve instead of immediate full-scale to reduce cost and oscillation risk
Keep financial cost component in the decision loop (cost_gradient) to prefer smaller, cheaper increments when economics justify it
Implement controller as a pluggable policy in the autoscaler service so other algorithms (ML predictor) can be swapped in later
tradeoffs: Stronger safety caps reduce blast radius but can increase observed SLA violations during massive bursts
Attenuation reduces overshoot but may increase time-to-recovery for sudden demand spikes
Quantile targeting improves SLA alignment at tails but requires careful smoothing to avoid noise-driven scale events
Adding a cost term improves unit economics but complicates controller tuning and makes response non-deterministic under identical loads
experiments: Synthetic burst tests in staging using JMeter scenario 'burst-5x-2m' to measure recovery characteristics
Chaos test: remove 20% of available GPUs during mid-burst to validate graceful fallback and admission controls
A/B test in dedicated pool: 5 tenants on Reservoir controller vs 5 on current step-scaler for 2 weeks, compare p95 latency, node-hours, and scale events
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (dev): library + unit tests, implement local sim harness (ETA 2w)
Phase 1 (staging): integrate into autoscaler, run deterministic burst sims and synthetic traffic (ETA 1w)
Phase 2 (canary): enable for low-risk tenants with conservative safety limits (ETA 2w)
Phase 3 (ramp): expand to 25% of Dedicated pools, monitor SLOs and cost metrics, run A/B analysis (ETA 4w)
Phase 4 (ga): full release with dashboard widgets and runbook updates (ETA dependent on metrics)
acceptance_criteria: In staging burst sims, p95 latency returns to baseline within 90s for 80% of scenarios
Node-hours consumed over baseline during A/B test is <= 15% while maintaining p95 SLOs for canary tenants
No increase in inter-tenant eviction incidents during canary period
Controller exposes debug traces and audit events for every scaling decision to the Console
